settings.headline: Dry eye isn't a moisture problem
settings.author: Thomas Cage
settings.lead: It sounds like it should be. The name says 'dry,' so you add moisture — drops, gels, more drops. And for an hour, it helps. Then you're gritty again. Here's the part almost nobody explains: for most people, dryness isn't the actual problem. Evaporation is.
settings.intro_body: Once you understand the difference, every drop that ever let you down suddenly makes sense — and so does what to do instead.
settings.reveal_title: The assumption that keeps you stuck
settings.reveal_intro: The whole category is built on one idea — that dry eye means not enough moisture. For the most common type of dry eye, that idea is simply wrong:
settings.myth_text: Dry eye means your eyes don't make enough tears — so the fix is to add more moisture with drops.
settings.fact_text: For most people the tears are there — they're just evaporating too fast, because the thin oil layer that's meant to seal them in has broken down. The problem isn't too little water. It's a missing lid on the jar.
settings.pullquote: Meibomian gland dysfunction — an oil-layer problem — is the leading cause of dry eye. Adding water to an evaporation problem is why the drops keep wearing off.
settings.why_title: Why the oil layer breaks down
settings.why_body: Tiny glands along your eyelid rims produce the oily top layer of your tears. With age they slow and clog, and hormonal shifts around perimenopause speed it up. Less oil reaches the surface, tears evaporate faster than they're replaced, and your eyes feel dry — even though the watery layer the drops top up was never really the issue.
settings.mech_intro: You don't fix an oil problem with water. You warm the oil so it flows again — which is exactly what Dewy is built to do.
settings.mech1_body: Research indicates the eyelid needs to reach around 40°C to soften the thickened oils in the glands. Dewy holds gentle, even warmth across the whole lid — not a flannel that's scalding then cold in 90 seconds.
settings.mech2_body: Warm compresses fail people because a hot towel is a nuisance. Dewy is a 10-minute ritual you'll actually repeat — consistency is the whole game.
settings.mech3_body: Comfortable enough to become the nice part of your evening rather than a chore. Comfort is what makes it a habit.
settings.mech4_body: Drops still have a place for the water layer. Dewy addresses the oil layer they can't reach — the two do different jobs, and many people use both.
